messages:
Anna: Heads up — DeltaTech reporting a big spike hitting their Dedicated pool `delta-prod`. Customers seeing 429s + some 503s, claiming TPS SLO breach. Asking for timeline and root cause.
Carlos: I saw the alerts. Runtime logs show `admission_control:rejected` 429s. Pattern looks like burst credits exhausted and autoscaler lag. Opening infra investigation.
Priya: How many tokens/sec were they sending? Any long context or big max_tokens? Need a repro payload.
Anna: Customer sent this repro script:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/delta-gen \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-delta-XXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"x","max_tokens":1024}'
```
They said ~60 concurrent requests/s, avg ~600 tokens/req -> ~36k tps sustained for short bursts.
Emily: Delta-prod pool configured for ~12k tps sustained; burst credits set to 50k minute window. Looks like they burned the credits. Admission control will reject once headroom threshold is crossed (we cap when headroom < 0.5).
infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale_requested 8->16 GPUs at 1764007925, scale_complete at 1764008370 (445s).
Josh: Autoscale cooldown is 300s; cold-provision and instance spin-up explains the ~7m gap where demand > capacity. We also saw high GPU memory churn.
Priya: Any sign of a noisy neighbor? Showed top sessions:
```
[2026-06-01T10:24:30Z] session_id=abc123 tokens/s=18000 model=redwood-13b customer=delta
[2026-06-01T10:24:32Z] session_id=def456 tokens/s=4000  model=redwood-13b customer=delta
[2026-06-01T10:24:35Z] session_id=ghi789 tokens/s=200  model=redwood-7b customer=internal-job
```
Looks like a single large job dominating with huge batch sizes.
Carlos: Mitigation applied now: 1) temp rate-cap via admission_control -> allow_rate=25k on delta-prod route 2) ops topped up burst credits to 75k 3) enforced route override to reduce delta max_tokens -> 512.
Anna: Customer also flagged unexpected billing spike (they were charged for burst usage) — finance review requested.
support-bot: Created billing review ticket BILL-1029 and assigned to Finance.
Emily: Action items — eng-runtime (Josh) to confirm admission_control thresholds and verify `X-Redwood-Admission` headers; infra (Carlos) to review autoscale timings and pre-warm options; Support (Anna) to send customer timeline and the temporary cap. I'll open a PR to shorten cooldown.
Josh: Quick repro I ran locally:
```
for i in `seq 1 60`; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/delta-gen -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-delta-REPRO" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"x","max_tokens":1024}' & done
```
Observed 429s with header `X-Redwood-Admission: rejected; reason=burst_depleted`, metrics snapshot: `tps=36000, headroom=-14k`.
Carlos: Short-term plan done. Monitoring shows 429s dropped ~90% after cap + burst top-up. Still seeing occasional 503s coincident with autoscale windows.
Anna: Sent customer status: "We applied temporary caps, increased burst credits, and started scaling fixes. ETA for config changes: ~24h. Finance reviewing billing." They acknowledged but asked for long-term headroom plan.
Priya: Long-term suggestions: set capacity target to peak * 1.25, enable pre-warm for scheduled events, add configurable burst purchase option on contract, and expose per-customer headroom telemetry. I'll draft recommendations.
Carlos: Follow-up — I lowered cooldown to 180s for delta-prod and left an ops note; pre-warm hooks queued for scheduled batch jobs. Watching metrics for 20m.
Anna: Update: 429s are now near zero; residual 503s only during scale transitions. Customer accepted temp config, wants formal SL adjustments + runbook for admission-control.
Priya: I'll prepare a short runbook: detection (tps > threshold + headroom <=0), mitigation (rate cap, reduce max_tokens, top-up burst, pre-warm) and postmortem checklist.
Anna: Thanks team. Closing once Finance confirms BILL-1029 resolution. :white_check_mark:
